spec_match.rationale: It puts the exact same keyword into radial-gradient() and circle() clip-path and reports each property's parse result separately, which is precisely the parity this feature ships.

interactive.rationale: Keyword toggles and centre sliders live-update two panels, a stacked overlay, generated CSS strings, and a per-property acceptance table.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises the boundary agreement 'which you can see, and which the demo measures' — the page measures the hand-computed fallback radius but never numerically measures whether the clip edge and the gradient's last stop coincide.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported branch is first-class: on a pre-155 browser the table shows gradient=yes / clip=no and the readout names the hand-computed pixel radius as the bug the feature removes.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5100672946143232 and CSS Images 3 radial gradients.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's radial-gradient-has-always-accepted-them assertion pins exactly the baseline this page demonstrates, alongside the shape-side positive and negative parses.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: clicked closest-corner, moved cx to 10%; table re-rendered 'radial-gradient yes (native) | clip-path no 102.1px (computed by hand)', computed backgroundImage confirmed the native gradient keyword applied; console clean, no exceptions, no failed same-origin requests; both viewport screenshots captured.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each render logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('parity-checked', …) with keyword and per-property support flags; no error events.

design_system.rationale: All colours come from tokens, keyword buttons flip background and color together via aria-pressed, and the match/mismatch cells use accent variables on light backgrounds.

accessibility.rationale: Real buttons with aria-pressed, labelled sliders, a captioned table with row/column scopes, and an aria-live output; the stacked comparison is also narrated by the table so the state is not visual-only.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 touch and at 1280x800 over CDP; screenshots at both widths show unclipped panels and 44px controls.

openQuestions.title: Measure the boundary agreement instead of asserting it
openQuestions.detail: The page claims the clip edge lands on the gradient's final stop and that the demo measures it, but no measurement of the rendered agreement exists — on a supporting browser both use the same native keyword and agreement is assumed. Sampling a canvas-drawn copy of the stacked box along the ray from the centre (find the gradient's last-stop distance vs the clip edge) would turn the claim into an observable, and would also expose real engine disagreements. Until then, softening the 'the demo measures' phrasing would be honest.

summary: The motivation demo works and degrades honestly: on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) the gradient accepts every corner keyword natively while clip-path rejects them, and the page states exactly that with the hand-computed fallback radius (102.1px at the tested centre). Controls, table, stacked overlay and generated CSS all verified over CDP at http://localhost:3000/v155/closest-corner-and-farthest-corner-radii-for-circle-and-ellipse-basic-shapes/gradient-parity/ with clean console and zero overflow on both device classes. Only real gap: the 'demo measures' claim about boundary coincidence is not actually measured.
